mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines a prime number?

options.A: A natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct positive divisors: 1 and itself.
options.B: A natural number that can be expressed as the product of two smaller natural numbers.
options.C: A natural number that has only one positive divisor.
options.D: A natural number that is divisible by 2.

mcqs.answer: A natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct positive divisors: 1 and itself.
mcqs.explanation: A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and the number itself, giving exactly two distinct divisors. Option B describes a composite number, C is false because every number has at least the divisor 1, and D is only true for even numbers, not all primes. Hence A is correct.

mcqs.question: Which of the following numbers is a composite number?
mcqs.explanation: A composite number has more than two positive divisors. The number 9 can be divided by 1, 3, and 9, so it has three divisors and is composite. Numbers 2, 3, and 5 each have exactly two divisors (1 and themselves) and are prime.

mcqs.question: Consider the numbers 14, 17, and 21. Which of the following correctly identifies each as prime or composite?

options.A: 14 is prime, 17 is composite, 21 is prime.
options.B: 14 is composite, 17 is prime, 21 is composite.
options.C: 14 is composite, 17 is composite, 21 is prime.

mcqs.answer: 14 is composite, 17 is prime, 21 is composite.
mcqs.explanation: 14 = 2 × 7 (more than two divisors) → composite. 17 has only 1 and 17 as divisors → prime. 21 = 3 × 7 → composite. Therefore option B correctly classifies each number. The other options mislabel at least one number.

mcqs.question: Why is the number 1 neither prime nor composite?

options.A: Because it has exactly one positive divisor, itself.
options.B: Because it is divisible by every integer.
options.C: Because it is larger than any prime number.
options.D: Because it can be written as a product of two different numbers.

mcqs.answer: Because it has exactly one positive divisor, itself.
mcqs.explanation: Prime numbers require exactly two distinct positive divisors (1 and the number), while composite numbers require more than two. The number 1 has only one divisor—1 itself—so it fits neither category. Options B, C, and D are incorrect statements about 1.

mcqs.learning_point: Find prime factors of a number
mcqs.question: What are the prime factors of 60?
mcqs.explanation: The prime factorisation of 60 is 2 × 2 × 3 × 5, so the prime factors (including multiplicities) are 2, 2, 3, and 5. Option A lists only the distinct primes, which is a common misconception. Options C and D are incorrect because they contain extra or wrong primes.

mcqs.question: If a number N is divisible by both 6 and 15, which of the following must be true about its prime factorisation?

options.A: N must contain the prime factor 2 at least once.
options.B: N must contain the prime factor 5 at least twice.
options.C: N must contain the prime factor 3 at least twice.
options.D: N must contain the prime factor 7.

mcqs.answer: N must contain the prime factor 2 at least once.
mcqs.explanation: Divisibility by 6 (2 × 3) ensures N includes at least one factor 2 and one factor 3. Divisibility by 15 (3 × 5) ensures at least one factor 3 and one factor 5. Therefore N must contain 2, 3, and 5 each at least once. Option A is guaranteed; B and C overstate the required multiplicities, and D is unrelated.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares prime and composite numbers?

options.A: A prime number has exactly two distinct positive divisors, whereas a composite number has more than two distinct positive divisors.
options.B: A prime number has only one divisor, while a composite number has exactly two.
options.C: Both prime and composite numbers have exactly two divisors.
options.D: Prime numbers are always odd, while composite numbers are always even.

mcqs.answer: A prime number has exactly two distinct positive divisors, whereas a composite number has more than two distinct positive divisors.
mcqs.explanation: By definition, a prime number possesses precisely two distinct positive divisors: 1 and itself. A composite number possesses more than two distinct positive divisors. Option B misstates the counts, C is false for composites, and D is incorrect because 2 is an even prime and many composites are odd.

mcqs.question: In competitive examinations, a composite number is defined as:

options.A: A natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct positive divisors.
options.B: A natural number greater than 1 that has more than two distinct positive divisors.
options.C: A natural number that is divisible only by 1 and itself.
options.D: A natural number that is a perfect square.

mcqs.answer: A natural number greater than 1 that has more than two distinct positive divisors.
mcqs.explanation: Competitive exam definitions align with the standard: a composite number is a natural number >1 with more than two positive divisors. Option A describes a prime number, C repeats the prime definition, and D describes a subset of composites (perfect squares) but not the full definition.
